notes: §1985:IX.4.2.4 GR5: "Following the successful execution of a CLOSE statement, the record area associated with file-name-1 is no longer available. The unsuccessful execution of such a CLOSE statement leaves the availability of the record area undefined." The rule withdraws a guarantee from the program and states no result for a reference to the area after the CLOSE, so it places no observable obligation on the implementation; what it needs is that the CLOSE completes and that nothing a later OPEN and READ deliver depends on the old content. EmitClose lowers every CLOSE (WITH LOCK included, which 85 accepts) to FileRegistry.CloseByFormat, which runs FileConnector.Close: the connector leaves its open mode and its store is flushed and disposed. The record area is a typed field of the emitted program for the life of the run unit, so after the CLOSE it keeps its last content (the determination docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-24 states for 2023's twin, GR-14.9.6.4-7), which the rule permits; there is no edition arm because 85 and 2023 differ only in the SAME RECORD AREA exception 2023 added, and the retained storage satisfies both. Probed at --std 85: after a successful CLOSE and after CLOSE WITH LOCK the area is readable and writable with no fault, an unsuccessful CLOSE (status 42) leaves it untouched, and a reopen and READ refill it. The witness closes an indexed file, checks status 00, reopens and reads the record back.

next.reason: 1985: "Following the successful execution of a CLOSE statement, the record area associated with file-name-1 is no longer available."; 2023: "the record area is available to the runtime element if any of the file connectors referenced by the other file-names in that SAME RECORD AREA clause are open". 2023 keeps unavailable-on-success and undefined-on-failure, but adds an exception: under SAME RECORD AREA the area stays available while another file in that clause is open.
